papers.title: Dinner invitation
lines: The Warden requests the pleasure of your company at High Table. Gowns will be worn.
Wine will be taken. Conversation will be had, mostly about conversation.

papers.title: Seaside postcard
lines: Having a lovely time. The sea is wet. The pier is long. The ice cream was stolen by a gull.
Wish you were here to guard the ice cream.

papers.title: Pilgrim's lead badge note
lines: Bought at the shrine for a farthing. It will protect me on the road home.
So far it has protected me from nothing, but the road is long and the inn has a roof.

papers.title: Ferry passenger's postcard
lines: Left France at dawn. England appeared as a long chalk line, as promised in the guidebook.
The customs man asked if I had anything to declare. I said: a deep, abiding love of tea.

trail.clue: A traveller buried a tin of sweets near the old oak in the eighties. 'For luck on the way back.'

papers.title: Hop-picking tally
lines: Six bushels today. Mum did eight, but she cheats and talks fast.
We camp in the huts. The men sing in the evening. It smells of hops and woodsmoke and the best week of the year.
